questions.question: When is a system of equations called a linear system?
options: At least one equation is quadratic.
Every equation in the system is linear.
The variables are written in alphabetical order.
The system has exactly two equations.

questions.question: How can a linear system be encoded compactly?
What are the three main objects in the matrix form of a linear system?
options: A coefficient matrix, an unknown vector, and a right-hand side.
A row vector, a transpose, and a trace.
A determinant, an eigenvalue, and an eigenvector.
A basis, a dimension, and a scalar field only.

questions.question: What method solves a linear system using an augmented matrix?
Can a system containing $xy=1$ be a system of linear equations in $x$ and $y$?
options: Yes, because it has an equals sign.
No, $xy$ is a product of unknowns.
No, because linear systems cannot have constants.
Yes, because it has two variables.

questions.question: Which is a linear system?
For $x+y=1$, $2x-y=0$, what are $A$ and $b$ in $Ax=b$ with unknowns $(x,y)^T$?
Which equation prevents the system from being linear?
A system has coefficient matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $b=\begin{pmatrix}3\\4\end{pmatrix}$. What equations does this represent?
Which augmented matrix belongs to the system $x-y=2$, $3x+y=5$?
Why can elementary row operations be used to solve a linear system?
options: They change the variables into nonlinear terms.
They remove the need for a right-hand side vector.
They give an equivalent system with the same solutions.
They only affect the names of the equations.

questions.question: What does it mean for a linear system to be transformed into standard form?
options: Variables aligned and a right-hand side constant.
The coefficient matrix is replaced by its inverse.

questions.question: Why is $Ax=b$ not just a shorthand for one equation when $A$ has several rows?
options: It represents one scalar equation for each row of $A$.
It represents only the first row of $A$.
It treats the columns of $A$ as unrelated constants.
It ignores the right-hand side vector.

questions.question: For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $b=\begin{pmatrix}5\\6\\7\end{pmatrix}$, how many equations and unknowns does $Ax=b$ represent?
Which system corresponds to $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\-1&3\end{pmatrix}$ and $b=\begin{pmatrix}4\\5\end{pmatrix}$?
Apply $R_2\leftarrow R_2-2R_1$ to the augmented matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\2&-1&0\end{pmatrix}$. What is the new second row?
Why does a linear system with the same $A$ but different $b$ keep the same left-hand side geometry but change the target?
options: $b$ fixes the coefficients, while $A$ gives the unknown names.
$A$ fixes the coefficients, while $b$ fixes the right-hand side values.
Changing $b$ changes the number of unknowns.
Changing $b$ forces all equations to become nonlinear.

questions.question: Why is a homogeneous system automatically a linear system only if its left-hand sides are linear?
options: Every equation with right-hand side zero is linear.
Linear systems must have nonzero right-hand side vectors.
Homogeneous systems cannot have more than one equation.
Zero right-hand sides don't make nonlinear left-hand sides linear.
